text:
Jamie: Heads up — EUW2 A10 prod is seeing p99 token latency ~2x higher since the last rollout (around 1864999000). Noticing it on low-latency routes only. :eyes:
Alex: ugh, thanks for flagging. Any correlation with PRs? link to rollout?
Jamie: rollout tracked to PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4123 — that merged last night. CI seemed green but prod started to diverge ~30m after.
Maria: did CI perf run catch anything?
dev-ci-bot: perf-check: a10-euw2-inference-suite — FAIL — p99 increase 95 -> 180 ms (+89%) on kernel-selection tests. Details: https://ci.redwood/12345
Jamie: attaching quick profile snapshot from a live A10 pod:
```
2026-03-16T21:10:02Z kernel_selector: picked kernel=v2_quant_opt for seq_len=128, batch=8
2026-03-16T21:10:02Z batch_handoff: ratio=0.9 -> preferring immediate handoff
2026-03-16T21:10:03Z kv_cache: evict_rate=0.33, miss_rate=0.12
2026-03-16T21:10:04Z nic_txq: drops=120, tx_packets=1.2M, rtt_ms=6

p50=20ms p95=60ms p99=180ms
```
Ling: that batch_handoff change stood out — default used to be 0.7 in our config. PR 4123 bumped it to 0.9 to improve amortized kernel reuse.
Alex: interesting — raising handoff ratio could increase KV cache churn if we hand off work before warm cache is used. Might explain evictions + miss spike.
Maria: were H100 clusters affected the same way? Any hw-diff?
Jamie: H100 in EUW2 didn't show the same jump. Only A10 pools (and a subset of L4) reported elevated p99. NIC stats show higher TX queue stalls on A10 nodes specifically.
sre-ops: looking at host metrics — A10 nodes in euw2-az2 show syscall wait spikes around the same time, and RX/TX backlog growth. Noisy neighbor? but increases align with the rollout window.
Alex: could be a combined effect: kernel_selector chose `v2_quant_opt` which increases per-request CPU/PCI work, and with higher handoff we pushed more short-lived batches causing many small NVMe/KV misses -> network bursts.
Ling: I ran a quick bisect locally: reverting the `batch_handoff` change in a branch reduces p99 back to baseline in a mini-repro. Not a full cluster test but suspicious.
Jamie: Agree. We should hold rollout for EUW2-A10 and maybe revert PR 4123 until we can measure.
Maria: +1 to hold. Also want a plan: capture kv cache traces, kernel selection logs and NIC txq histograms for a 1h window during the revert.
Alex: I'll open a revert PR and a targeted rollback for euw2-A10. Also adding a flag to keep batch_handoff at 0.7 for rollout gating.
Alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4130 (revert batch_handoff bump)
Jamie: testing note: to reproduce use the following traffic pattern (short seq len, many small requests):
```bash
wrk -t8 -c100 -d60s --latency http://a10-euw2.test/generate -s scripts/short-requests.lua
```
Maria: good. I'll schedule a gated canary once revert is in. Also suggest enabling kv debug logs for canary only.
Ling: for follow-up, we should also profile kernel_selector hot paths on A10 vs H100. The kernel chosen seems fine, but the resource interaction looks different on A10.
sre-ops: noted. I'll snapshot NIC counters and enable tcp info export for the canary window.
dev-ci-bot: perf-check queued for PR 4130. Staging run will include a10-euw2 and h100-usw2 suites.
Jamie: timeline?
Alex: opening PR now, aiming to deploy revert to euw2-A10 within 30m, full rollout hold until we confirm.
Maria: tagging infra for additional observability: @sre-ops please add `kv.debug=1` and `kernel_selector.trace=1` for the canary hosts.
sre-ops: done — flags set for 5 nodes in canary pool.
Jamie: thanks. If this reverts p99 we can iterate on a safer handoff algorithm (maybe adaptive by measured cache hit rate).
Alex: noted — propose adaptive threshold: if kv miss_rate > 0.05 then keep handoff_ratio <= 0.75. We'll draft a follow-up PR with metrics-based gating.
Ling: also adding a test in our CI perf suite that runs A10-specific microbench to catch this hardware-specific regression earlier.
Jamie: ok, will monitor. Please post results here once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
